title: Lazy-loading media elements fire loadstart and reject source candidates before deferring, unlike Chrome
body:
The [resource selection algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-media-load-algorithm)'s synchronous section runs regardless of the [lazy loading attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#lazy-loading-attribute):

> ⌛ Set the media element's `networkState` to `NETWORK_LOADING`.
>
> ⌛ Queue a media element task given the media element to fire an event named `loadstart` at the media element.

...and in *children* mode, `source` candidates are checked and rejected there too:

> ⌛ If candidate has a `type` attribute whose value, when parsed as a MIME type (including any codecs described by the `codecs` parameter, for types that define that parameter), represents a type that the user agent knows it cannot render, then end the synchronous section, and jump down to the *failed with elements* step below.

Only the [resource fetch algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-media-load-resource) parks:

> If the will lazy load element steps given the media element return true: … Return.

So for a below-viewport `loading=lazy` video, the spec has `networkState` at `NETWORK_LOADING`, `loadstart` fired, and `error` fired at any `source` with an unsupported `type`, all before the element is ever scrolled into view.

In Chrome Canary, none of that appears to happen while the video is below the viewport: `networkState` is `NETWORK_IDLE` by the time the `load` event fires, and no `loadstart` or `source` `error` events fire. Once the video is scrolled into view, `loadstart` and the `source` `error` fire and the load proceeds. The existing wpt tests [video-loading-lazy-to-eager.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-video-element/video-loading-lazy-to-eager.html) and [video-loading-lazy-not-rendered.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-video-element/video-loading-lazy-not-rendered.html) assert that `loadstart` doesn't fire while lazy, matching Chrome rather than the spec.

Maybe the lazy check should be earlier in the resource selection algorithm, with the resumption steps covering candidate selection too?

(Found while writing a test for #12971.)
